content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding WSGI and ASGI Architecture in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When deploying Flask applications, understanding the underlying server communication interfaces is crucial for performance, scalability, and modern feature support. This tutorial covers WSGI, ASGI, and how Flask adapts to both architectures."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is WSGI?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Web Server Gateway Interface (WSGI), defined in PEP 3333, is a standardized specification for how web servers communicate with Python web applications. WSGI is synchronous, meaning it handles one request per thread at a time."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Synchronous request-response cycle."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Traditional standard for Python web frameworks like Flask and Django."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Well-supported by production servers like Gunicorn and uWSGI."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"What is ASGI?"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface (ASGI) is the modern successor to WSGI. It is designed to handle asynchronous programming paradigms in Python, supporting WebSockets, HTTP/2, and long-polling in addition to standard HTTP requests."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Asynchronous by design, leveraging Python's async and await syntax."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supports multiple protocols including HTTP, WebSockets, and background tasks."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Powered by servers like Uvicorn, Hypercorn, and Daphne."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Running Flask on WSGI"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, Flask is a WSGI application. You can run a Flask application in production using a WSGI server such as Gunicorn."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"pip install gunicorn\ngunicorn -w 4 'app:create_app()'"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Adapting Flask for ASGI"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because Flask is inherently synchronous, it does not natively process requests asynchronously out-of-the-box like FastAPI. However, Flask applications include an ASGI scope wrapper (wsgi_app) that allows them to run on ASGI servers like Uvicorn."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"pip install uvicorn\nuvicorn app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"While WSGI remains reliable for standard blocking HTTP applications in Flask, moving to an ASGI server like Uvicorn opens up possibilities for modern deployment topologies, event loops, and hybrid applications."}]
